subject: Intermittent OOMs on edge: dynamic windowing + SDK batching edge-case
messages:
From: Erin Moss <erin.moss@cloudpath.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: support@cloudpath.com
Date: Fri, 12 Oct 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden OOMs after SDK update (edge cluster)

Hi Mateo / Sean,

We started seeing intermittent OOMs on three of our edge hosts after upgrading to SDK v1.9.2 last night. Errors look like host-level OOM kills tied to the inference process. We've attached a heap profile and an SDK trace.

High level:
- Failures are bursty — tend to appear when we see short bursts of high concurrency (50-120 reqs/s) on the smallest instance type (g4dn.x).
- Process memory climbs quickly and the runtime is killed within ~30s.
- Rolling back the SDK to v1.9.0 reduces frequency but doesn't eliminate the issue.

We reproduced locally in our staging edge cluster and captured the traces. Given this is production impacting, can your team triage? We suspect something with the dynamic batch/window recalculation in the client-side SDK interacting badly with connection churn.

Attachments: heap_profile_20281012.txt (6MB, text stub), sdk_trace_20281012.log (2MB), screenshot-oom.png

Thanks,
Erin Moss
SRE, CloudPath

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Erin Moss <erin.moss@cloudpath.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Oct 2028 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden OOMs after SDK update (edge cluster)

Erin — thanks for the trace and heap profile. I pulled this into our inbox and started an initial pass. Quick notes and asks so we can triage with runtime: 

1) Can you confirm your SDK config flags for windowing/batching (exact JSON)? particularly any non-default values for: window_scaler, min_window_ms, max_window_tokens, pref_batch_timeout_ms.
2) If you can reproduce in staging, could you run the attached repro script (I put a copy in the Drive link) with TRACE=runtime and leave it running for ~10 min so we capture pre-oom snapshots?
3) We will attempt a workaround on our side: temporarily disable the SDK dynamic scaler and fall back to fixed windowing to see if that stabilizes memory. Would you allow us to coordinate a brief change (5–10 minutes) on one staging host?

Looping in Karthik from runtime for deeper investigation. Sean — flagging this as a high-impact CloudPath account for prioritization and possible credits if this is regressional.

Mateo Alvarez
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Oct 2028 10:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden OOMs after SDK update (edge cluster)

Thanks for the signal and the artifacts, Erin / Mateo. Quick read on the logs: I see a pattern where the SDK repeatedly collapses a window (to very small token budgets) then quickly re-expands, creating many tiny batches back-to-back. That combined with frequent connection churn causes multiple KV cache duplications in memory. Two hypotheses: 

- Race in client window recalculation when a request is canceled and reissued (we saw cancel+retry traces).
- On memory-constrained hosts the runtime's async cleanup of KV caches is delayed, so transient duplicated caches accumulate and push memory over the limit.

Immediate asks from runtime: 
- Erin: can you share the SDK client config JSON (non-default flags) and the exact repro CLI command you used?
- Heap dump good — can you also attach a timeline of process restarts (system logs) for the same window? we need to correlate timestamps.

Short-term mitigation I can try from our side: add a fast-path GC trigger for duplicated KV references (not ideal, but should reduce peak). Workaround you can apply now: set client flag "window_scaler": 0 (disable dynamic scaling) and increase "min_window_ms" to 50ms to reduce micro-batching. Mateo / Sean: is exposing those flags via the public SDK config an acceptable product ask? If so, we should track it.

I'll reproduce this in our internal cluster with the same memory profile and post findings by EOD.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Runtime
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Oct 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden OOMs after SDK update (edge cluster)

Quick commercial/context note: CloudPath runs a real-time video ingestion pipeline — 30s of downtime per host materially affects their SLA. If this is SDK-regression-related we should be prepared to:

- Offer a one-week trial credit while we stabilize (ask from Marissa on discount authority).
- Ship a documented SDK flag workaround (clear instructions + example) and a simple CLI to flip flags on staging hosts.
- Track a product story to make the smoothing flag first-class in the SDK (expose via config object and document tuning guidance).

Karthik: please prioritize reproduction and a minimal mitigation. Mateo: I'll own the customer comms and draft the mitigation steps for CloudPath once you confirm the approved workaround.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Erin Moss <erin.moss@cloudpath.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, support@cloudpath.com
Date: Sat, 13 Oct 2028 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden OOMs after SDK update (edge cluster)

Thanks all — I ran the workaround on one staging host (window_scaler=0 + min_window_ms=50) and left it under load for 20 minutes. No OOM during the test period. I attached the updated heap profile and the execution command we used.

Command we ran: ./loadtest --sdk-config '{"window_scaler":0, "min_window_ms":50, "max_window_tokens":1024}' --concurrency 80

We're okay with the temporary workaround and appreciate the fast triage. Please keep us posted on the root cause and planned SDK/API changes; we need a roadmap ETA to communicate to ops.

Erin
SRE, CloudPath
